'''''Zhengheornis''''' ({{lit|[[Zhenghe County|Zhenghe]] bird}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[Basal (phylogenetics)|basal]] [[avialan]] known from the [[Late Jurassic]] ([[Kimmeridgian]]–[[Tithonian]] ages) [[Nanyuan Formation]] of China.The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Zhengheornis buyu''''', known from a partial skeleton with feather traces, preserved on a [[Compression fossil|slab and counterslab]].

== Discovery and naming ==
The ''Zhengheornis'' fossil material was discovered during fieldwork from March to April 2024, in outcrops of the [[Nanyuan Formation]] ('layer 6') near Yangyuan Village of [[Zhenghe County]], [[Fujian Province]], China. The specimen is housed in the [[Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology]] (IVPP), where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen IVPP V34168. It consists of a partial articulated skeleton with associated feather traces, preserved as a [[compression fossil|slab and counterslab]]. Known material includes much of the post-{{dinogloss|cervical}} vertebral column, part of the {{dinogloss|pelvis}}, and much of the forelimbs and hindlimbs, much of which is preserved as molds.<ref name="Zhengheornis" />

In 2026, Min Wang and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Zhengheornis buyu'' as a new genus and species of early avialan dinosaur based on these fossil remains, establishing IVPP V34168 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Zhengheornis'', combines a reference to the discovery of the only known specimen in Zhenghe County, with the [[Greek language|Greek]] word {{lang|grc|ornis}}, meaning {{gloss|bird}}. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''buyu'', is a [[Mandarin Chinese|Mandarin]] word meaning {{gloss|unexpected}}, referencing the distinctive morphology of the pelvis and tail of this species.<ref name="Zhengheornis" />

To test the affinities and relationships of ''Zhengheornis'', Wang et al. (2026) included it in an updated version of the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of Chen et al. (2025).<ref name="Baminornis" /> ''Zhengheornis'' was recovered as a member of the [[Avialae]], diverging after [[Anchiornithidae]] and ''[[Archaeopteryx]]'', but immediately before the coeval ''[[Baminornis]]''.<ref name="Zhengheornis" /> Later that year, Xu et al. named ''[[Yuezhuornis]]'', another avialan from the Nanyuan Formation. Using the matrix of Wang et al., they recovered ''Yuezhuornis'' and ''Zhengheornis'' as [[sister taxa]], a clade they named [[Zhengheornithidae]]. == Paleoecology ==
''Zhengheornis'' is known from the Nanyuan Formation, which dates to around {{ma|150}},<ref name="Zhengheornis" /> around the border between the [[Kimmeridgian]] and [[Tithonian]] ages of the late [[Jurassic]] period. The outcrops of this formation have been interpreted as representing a primarily [[swamp]]-like [[depositional environment]]. Most of the vertebrate fossils from the formation represent aquatic and semiaquatic animals, including indeterminate unnamed [[teleost]] fish, [[turtles]], and [[choristoderes]]. Some avialan dinosaur fossils have also been discovered, including the [[anchiornithid]] ''[[Fujianvenator]]'', the closely related ''[[Yuezhuornis]]'',<ref name="Yuezhuornis" /> the more derived ''[[Baminornis]]'',<ref name="Baminornis"/> and some additional indeterminate birds, including a possible [[ornithuromorph]] known from a [[furcula]]. This [[lagerstätte]] is collectively referred to as the Zhenghe Fauna.<ref name="Fujianvenator" />
